title: The canonical degree-zero base-change map is invertible
statement: Let X,S,X\prime,S\prime be schemes [def-pc-scheme], f:X\to S a proper flat morphism locally of finite presentation [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let g:S\prime\to S, g\prime:X\prime\to X, f\prime:X\prime\to S\prime form a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume module categories on X and X\prime have injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let M be an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], with R^0 f_* M invertible and R^q f_* M=0 for q>0 [def-pc-invertible-in-degree-zero]. Write c:g\prime^*f^*\cong f\prime^*g^* for the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then the map beta:g^*f_* M\to f\prime_*g\prime^*M adjoint to c^{-1} followed by g\prime^*(epsilon_M) under the canonical pullback/pushforward adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] is an isomorphism.
